newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes up as blue chips stage comeback.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes up as blue chips stage comeback.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index recovered from early losses at Monday's price fixing led by a late comeback from the bourse's most heavily capitalised issues.

Komercni Banka pulled back from a 14 crown loss at the fixing to close down five to 2,365 and CEZ, which was down two, recovered to end the day unchanged on 1,064. SPT Telecom built on small early gains to close up 17 crowns to 3,390.
Dealers said the stagnatory character of the market in recent sessions made it difficult to predict its direction in the short term but were convinced that the PX50 still had strong upside potential.
"The flow of money into the market is now quite difficult to predict...(but) I think the market still has good potential to rise," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.
In the broader market there were some typically volatile swings from low liquidity issues. Brewery Pivovar Radegast lost 50 crowns to 5,450 while Prazske Pivovary rose 55 crowns to 2,325.
Computer systems company PVT, fell 181 crowns to 3,458 and conference oraganiser BVV Brno rose 50 crowns to 3,500.
Overall, turnover was relatively high at 1.7 billion crowns.
